subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a first-party `backup.target` / `backup.encryption.key` encrypted folder snapshot flow once the security blockers and proof gap are fixed?
rationale: The PR adds new user-facing backup commands and config/secrets surface rather than only repairing the existing archive command, so code review cannot decide the permanent product boundary alone.

options.title: Sponsor native snapshots after blockers
options.body: Accept the direction only after the path-hardening findings, upgrade/security proof, and real CLI smoke evidence are complete.

options.title: Keep core to archives
options.body: Decline the new config-backed snapshot flow and keep broader backup work tracked by the existing backup/restore issues.

options.title: Split into narrower work
options.body: Land only archive/restore hardening separately and require a smaller follow-up design for folder snapshots.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native snapshots after blockers
recommendation.body: Accept the direction only after the path-hardening findings, upgrade/security proof, and real CLI smoke evidence are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main history shows broad ownership of the current CLI/provider refactor surface this PR would integrate with.
